communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: NICB Emails
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

All emails, including attachments, sent or received by Riverside County District Attorney’s Office employee John Gubernat in which any sender or recipient (To, From, CC or BCC) has an email address ending in @nicb.org, and which contain any of the following terms anywhere in the subject line, body or attachments:

“Flock”
“LPR”
“ALPR”

Date range: January 1, 2024 through the date this request is processed.

This request needs a search of one mailbox only (John Gubernat’s), filtered by sender/recipient domain (@nicb.org) and the keywords above. I am not asking for an office-wide search.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jason Hunyar

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: LexisNexis and Appriss Contracts
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

1. Active or past (last 3 years) Contracts you have with LexisNexis (including RELX or LexisNexis Risk Solutions). If you have multiple contracts, we are specifically seeking anything relating to Accurint, Accurint Virtual Crime Center, DORS, or BuyCrash. If you hold a file called an XML Addendum (sometimes called an AVCC/ACA Addendum) please include this document, otherwise the basic signed/executed contract will suffice. 

2. Active or past (last 3 years) contracts you have with Appriss (or parent company Equifax) relating to the VINELink, VINE, or similar jail information sharing platforms. 

3. Any contracts or data sharing agreements/MOUs you have that involve the sharing of JMS data with third parties (whether government or private). If your JMS has any type of interface or active data sharing, please include an agreement document relating to the interface.

I also request that, if appropriate, fees be waived as we believe this request is in the public interest, as suggested but not stipulated by the recommendations of the Massachusetts Supervisor of Public Records. The requested documents will be made available to the general public free of charge as part of the public information service at MuckRock.com, and is not made for commercial usage.

I expect the request to be filled in an accessible format, including for screen readers, which provide text-to-speech for persons unable to read print. Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf image files as well as physical documents.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Shawn Segal
